newsitem.title: FRANCE: Major says UK won't be in EMU first wave - paper.
newsitem.headline: Major says UK won't be in EMU first wave - paper.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Monday Britain would clearly not take part in economic and monetary union (EMU) if it started on time, according to an interview in French daily Le Figaro.

He said it was highly unlikely, if not impossible, that the different European Union (EU) countries would be able to post sufficiently clear and stable economic performances to meet the Maastricht criteria, and he believed the European Union would postpone the project.
"But, if in spite of everything it sees the light of day, it's clear that we will not be part of it," Major was quoted as saying.
Major said Labour Party opposition leader Tony Blair was perhaps perceived by other EU members as being more in favour of the social policies they wanted to introduce.
"I challenge these policies which I judge to be dangerous for European competitivity and for jobs," he said.
He said Europe was making a mistake pursuing policies of centralisation and integration and that it would only find its way by respecting national traditions and cultures.
"Europe would be going in the wrong direction. I will continue to fight to prevent this from happening," Major said.
Major said, however, that if the ruling Conservatives were re-elected there was no question of them pulling out of the EU and seeking a free trade agreement.

"Britain belongs to the union. It has an interest in staying there and it is perfectly within in its rights at the heart of the debate on the future of (European) construction," he was quoted as saying.
Major also said that Labour Party policies would lead towards more centralisation within Europe and jeopardise the recent performance of Britain.
